response.content:
For a stationary pion decaying into two bodies, momentum is conserved, so the muon and neutrino have equal and opposite momenta.

Taking the neutrino as effectively massless:

\[
E_\mu=\frac{m_\pi^2+m_\mu^2}{2m_\pi}
=\frac{139.6^2+105.7^2}{2(139.6)}
\approx 109.82\text{ MeV}
\]

So,

\[
KE_\mu=E_\mu-m_\mu=109.82-105.7\approx 4.12\text{ MeV}
\]

The neutrino energy is:

\[
E_\nu=139.6-109.82\approx 29.8\text{ MeV}
\]

Since the neutrino is massless, this is its kinetic energy. Thus the kinetic energies are approximately \(4.12\text{ MeV}\) and \(29.8\text{ MeV}\).

Answer: B
